questions.q: Which hostname routes to the isolated northbridge-aks-prod cluster?
options: dev.shop.northbridgeretail.com
staging.shop.northbridgeretail.com
shop.northbridgeretail.com
northbridge-prod.internal
questions.explain: shop.northbridgeretail.com routes to the northbridge-prod namespace on the isolated northbridge-aks-prod cluster, while dev and staging hostnames both route to namespaces on the shared northbridge-aks-dev cluster.

questions.q: What does cert-manager do in Northbridge's ingress setup?
options: Manually stores a certificate uploaded by an engineer
Automates TLS certificate issuance and renewal from an issuer like Let's Encrypt, based on an Ingress annotation
Replaces the NGINX Ingress Controller entirely
Generates the Azure AD federated identity credentials
questions.explain: cert-manager watches the cluster-issuer annotation on an Ingress resource and automatically requests and renews a certificate, populating the TLS secret without manual steps.

questions.q: How does the checkout pod authenticate to Azure Key Vault without a stored secret?
options: It reads a client secret baked into the container image
Azure AD Workload Identity federation lets its Kubernetes service account exchange its own token for an Azure AD token, trust scoped by a federated identity credential
It uses the cluster's root kubeconfig credentials
Key Vault is configured to allow anonymous access from the dev VNet
questions.explain: A federated identity credential trusts tokens from the specific service account, namespace, and AKS OIDC issuer, letting the pod obtain an Azure AD token with nothing stored.

questions.q: What role does External Secrets Operator play for Northbridge's workloads?
options: It issues TLS certificates in place of cert-manager
It syncs secrets from Key Vault into native Kubernetes Secret objects on a refresh interval, so pods mount Secrets normally
It replaces Terraform for provisioning Key Vault
It stores secrets directly inside Helm values.yaml files for versioning
questions.explain: External Secrets Operator reads from Key Vault and writes native Kubernetes Secrets, so application pods keep mounting Secret volumes while the source of truth stays in Key Vault, not Git.

questions.q: Why doesn't the azure/login step in Northbridge's GitHub Actions workflow include a client-secret field?
options: Azure login never requires any credential, even in production
The federated identity credential trusts GitHub's OIDC token issuer, scoped to the repo and branch, so no stored Azure client secret exists to leak
The client secret is instead stored as a GitHub Secret and referenced separately
GitHub Actions bypasses authentication for internal repos
questions.explain: A federated identity credential trusts tokens issued by https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com for a specific repo/ref, letting azure/login exchange that OIDC token for an Azure AD token with no stored client secret.
